newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Key Ebos shareholder sells down.
newsitem.headline: Key Ebos shareholder sells down.

text.p: EBOS Group said on Tuesday its 50 percent shareholder cut its stake in a move to diversify holdings, and that the acquisition of Sydney's Richard Thompson and Co had been concluded.
Investment company Whyte Adder, run by EBOS director Peter Kraus on behalf of his family trust, will remain the largest shareholder by retaining 20 percent of EBOS.

The off market trade of 2.5 million shares was crossed by Ord Minnett Securities at $5.60 and accounted for more than half the sharemarket's total $23.6 million trading value today, which was reduced by holidays in Auckland and Australia.
The stock closed down 27 cents at $6.08 on Monday.
Managing director of the Christchurch hospital supply company, Mark Waller, told NZPA Kraus had planned the selldown for some time.
"He's really just for his own personal reasons been looking to diversify his own portfolio," Waller said.
The move would increase liquidity in EBOS stock, with no new shareholder owning more than 5 percent, he said.
"We're pretty pleased about it because we've never been totally comfortable with having effectively one person like that controlling 50-odd percent of the company."
Commenting on the large variation in the stock price, Waller said EBOS did not know the trade would go through on Monday and institutions looked for a 5-10 percent discount before buying.

Late last year Ebos said it would buy medical wholesaler Richard Thompson for $4.07 million subject to shareholder and Australian Foreign Investment Review Board approval . It said then payment would be $2.74 million in cash plus an issue of 250,000 ordinary Ebos shares valued at $1.31 million.
